correctness.rationale: For each fixed leaf set and nonleaf core, the Prüfer multinomial degree count and a product of formal leaf-allocation series give the exact coefficient formula. Differentiating at y=1 gives explicit Stirling ratios for both conditional factorial moments. A core path realizes exactly every prescribed leaf-load vector with at least two positive entries. Strict boundary cases m=1 and n=3 are handled separately. The standalone exact checker independently reproduces all joint coefficients and support for n=3 to 8 (90 finite assertions). The infinite claim rests on the analytic bijection, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus and literature searches identified closely related uniform-tree degree and local-pattern results, but no matching all-size joint distribution conditioned on the leaf count. The strongest inspected primary comparison on fully labelled Cayley trees proves asymptotic normality of pattern counts, not this finite bivariate polynomial. The other primary studies use binary trees with leaf-only labels and different measures. Unsearched older general-purpose tree-generating formulas remain a priority risk; absence of a match is not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unidentified general labelled-tree two-sort or attachment generating function might already imply the finite polynomial, even without using sibling-leaf terminology.
Not every indexed or older graph-enumeration database or textbook was exhaustively searched; priority is provisional.

value.rationale: It is a complete finite-sample joint law for two standard structural aspects of uniform fully labelled trees: endpoint abundance and shared-neighbour clustering. The exact conditional mean and variance and full attainable-value support permit nonasymptotic tree-shape null calibration. The statistic depends on leaf adjacencies, so it is not just a renaming of the classical Prüfer degree count or a cherry table for degree-three binary phylogenetic trees; scope is natural and no artificial parameter slices are introduced.
